cluster_name: Iran president says contact with Supreme Leader Khamenei 'very difficult'
event_summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in a state television interview that communication with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is currently 'very difficult'; Khamenei has not appeared publicly since the US-Israeli strike that killed his father and reportedly wounded him.
tldr: Iran International—citing sources—reported that Pezeshkian was taken to a secret Tehran location and permitted only minutes in a dark, tinted-window car with a man presented as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, raising unresolved questions about whether Khamenei is genuinely incapacitated. Pezeshkian's own public admission that reaching Khamenei is very difficult is the first official Iranian acknowledgment of a communications gap that opposition media has alleged since the February 2026 US-Israeli strike. Iran state media—IRNA and Tehran Times—covers none of this, instead running Pezeshkian statements on Palestinian solidarity and an upcoming presidential television interview series, a pointed editorial contrast with the rest of the corpus. US right-wing outlet Breitbart uniquely ties the leadership communications breakdown to the timeline of the ongoing Hormuz Strait negotiations.

evidence.quote: Pezeshkian, however, defended Khamenei against rising speculation over his absence from public view.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has warned President Masoud Pezeshkian that his next resignation would be accepted, a relative of Khamenei by marriage said in a video released Monday, prompting sharp denials and political backlash.
Khamenei, who was wounded in the U.S.-Israeli strike that launched the Middle East war, has not appeared in public since succeeding his father, who was killed in the same attack.
The comments followed a report by Iran’s Tabnak media site on Monday saying that Khamenei warned Pezeshkian that he (Khamenei) would accept the Iranian president's resignation if he resubmits it.
Pezeshkian defended his leader, insisting he had held productive meetings with him and had been met with "kindness and very sound logic."

bottom_line: Pezeshkian's public admission that reaching Mojtaba Khamenei is 'very difficult' is the first official Iranian acknowledgment of a leadership accessibility gap that opposition sources have alleged since Khamenei was wounded in the February 2026 US-Israeli strike. Iran state media's conspicuous silence on this story—redirecting to Palestinian solidarity—signals a deliberate effort to project institutional normalcy while the opposition and Western press focus on whether Iran's Supreme Leader is genuinely incapacitated.
